children: Biogen was pacing toward a two-year closing high on Monday after J.P. Morgan upgraded the shares, pointing to a rich slate of upcoming clinical-trial catalysts.

Shares climbed 4.1% to $235.04 after analyst Chris Schott raised his rating on Biogen to Overweight from Neutral with a $300 price target, up from $210. If those gains hold, Biogen will end the session at its highest level since July 2024, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The bullish call comes ahead of prospective milestones next year, namely data readouts for a handful of pipeline candidates. Among them, Schott highlighted felzartamab, a monoclonal antibody acquired through Biogen's $1.8 billion buyout of Human Immunology Biosciences in 2024.

A Phase 2 trial of 22 patients with antibody-mediated rejection — a condition where a recipient's immune system rejects a transplanted kidney — showed promise. Over 80% of trial participants taking felzartamab showed resolution on their biopsies, compared with just 20% on a placebo.
This result suggests felzartamab could be "transformative" for the roughly 11,000 patients affected by the condition, Schott wrote. Late-stage trial data is slated for the first half of next year.

If felzartamab ultimately secures Food and Drug Administration approval, Schott anticipates rapid uptake due to limited effective treatments for AMR, a "relatively straightforward patient identification process," and an experienced sales team gained through Biogen's recent acquisition of Apellis.

The analyst believes felzartamab could easily generate $2 billion a year treating kidney transplant rejection alone, though the opportunity could be "potentially much larger" if the drug proves to be effective in other indications.

Biogen's name is primarily associated with Leqembi, an Alzheimer's drug co-developed with Eisai. It has been a slow-but-steady grower since its launch in 2023, with analysts anticipating it to generate more substantial revenue in coming quarters.

While felzartamab could be arguably Biogen's biggest opportunity, Biogen has more in the pipeline. The company is set to release data from two Phase 3 clinical trials evaluating litifilimab for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in the fourth quarter of this year.

Developing drugs for SLE is notoriously difficult. Symptoms vary widely among patients and past clinical trials across the industry have shown unpredictable results, meaning any trial carries elevated risk. This view is "widely shared by investors," Schott wrote, adding that "there are several pipeline catalysts where we have far higher conviction set to report shortly after litifilimab's SLE data."
Consequently, he believes "it makes sense" to own Biogen heading into the SLE data readout, "with shares likely to quickly recover on any setbacks with the program and rally on positive results."

Shares have surged 33% this year, outpacing a 19% gain for the iShares Biotechnology exhange-traded fund, of which Biogen is a component. An increasingly compelling series of growth drivers and a clearer path to long-term growth could help those gains continue, but whether the analyst's high expectations materialize remains to be seen.
